items.q: Dizzy, Stan Getz, you know, Blakey’s band - cause he was a melody freak – Herbie, Wayne, you know.

ctx.x: this. Then the guys, the white guys are looking at Joey, “Yeah, one of us, yeah.” You know? “Yeah, he’s playing it too.” You know, so he’s like Elvis. You know what I mean? So, and then there’s people watching Justin. “How old is that kid. Aw, he’s amazing.” And we play these songs. And we play with a lot of energy on certain songs and we played energetic songs and pretty songs. That’s kind of what we do, energy and pretty and it’s a good combination. It works well. But I understand that eighty percent of the…

melodies. Not the guys who played the best solos. It was the guys who played the best melodies. Dizzy, Stan Getz, you know, Blakey’s band - cause he was a melody freak – Herbie, Wayne, you know. It always was the same guys. When he was alive, Duke.
You mentioned earlier that the experiences you had working with Sting and working in the television show had a – now I have to paraphrase you – let’s just say, had a profound impact on you.
